interactions.title: Govir’s account of discovery, captivity and hope
lines: DM: Okay. So, as the noise of the battle echoes above—the sound of fists hitting flesh, the crack of the rope ladder leaping and lunging at its enemies, the snarls of wolfish creatures—a man in a dirty torn robe crouches among the empty barrels of this basement store.

DM: With the scent of blood, an image flashes through his mind: leaning over a dead body, tearing at flesh. He's briefly overcome imagining leaping up, letting the wild strength rush over his body, reveling in the power as his hands grow to claws, his teeth to fangs. But, like so many times before, he pushes the desire away, muttering a soft prayer to Jeevali to keep him safe, to keep him in control. He thinks of the nightmare his life has become, in the past month, not daring yet to hope his unexpected rescuers may yet succeed, winning not just the battle above but finding a cure for his curse.

DM: A month ago, he was riding high on the joy of discovery after Hada uncovered letters from Commander Ila and a map. Here was a chance to do some real exploring, to uncover the mysteries that surrounded the Fraternity of the Empty Moon. The gods are great and would lead him to knowledge, surely. Of course he rushed off with Hada to explore, stopping only to ask the old veterans at Darshana's if they knew anything more. Who could wait when the thrill of discovery was right there?

DM: Getting to the old fort was easy, following the map. Little was left: just two of the four corner towers and a great gash in the earth. Yet strangely that gash could not be approached, not without a gray fog and confusion enveloping his thoughts till he found himself wandering far away, confused and disoriented. If only he and Hada had not had a long conversation right there about the map, what might be missing, what more they could maybe find in the archives, that would reveal the secrets of why the instructions written on this map did not seem to work. For one of the beasts must have been listening, perhaps hidden in the tower ruins.

DM: Then the terror of the attack. Just flashes dance through the man's memory: waking to a silent wolf human hybrid as its jaws closed around his arm; passing out; waking briefly to see Dag, one of the dwarf kids, dead and bleeding in the hall; then fainting to blessed darkness. Then coming to consciousness in an underground cell, strangely lit, though all color is bleached from the world. A blur of pain and blood loss, only the grace of the gods keeping him sane. Constantly being asked, ‘What’s missing? What’s—how do we get into the gash itself?’ A sense of urgency.

DM: Then silence, leaving him alone, no food, little water. The big guard keeps poking him and laughing, “Soon you'll get all the food you want, and once you taste flesh, there is no going back.” Then just blackness. A day? More? Hard to know until he wakes back in this cell, the gnawed bones of Hada strewn around. If he knew the secret to the map, the clue that must be missing, he would tell them. He already suggested magic, perhaps invisible ink. It gets harder to resist the blackness; he knows it's creeping across his soul. He's not sure he can survive another night of the full moon, and certainly not two. He prays constantly to the gods; he does not know if they can hear him in this dark place.

DM: Until those strangers appeared, glowing in a magical light, slaughtering his captors. That Dunmari man Kenzo seems possessed of an inner light. Like the warm embrace of Bhishma telling him, he was found again, of Shakun telling him, he was protected. Maybe these are the answer to his prayers after all. The story spills out of him. Why hold back when talking to the servants of the gods?

DM: Mind jumps back to the present as the sounds of battle fade. For a moment terror grips him, for he knows not who won. Then the reassuring clatter of the rope ladder that miraculously came to life at the command of the dwarf tells him he might really be saved, and gratitude for Jeevali, for Laka, Bhishma, Shakun, for the whole divine family fills his heart. He pauses praying silently, staying hidden until told otherwise as we drift back to the dining hall, the dead bodies, scattered papers tossed off the table and our four adventurers standing, catching your breath after the battle.
